page: Google Cloud Platform z3-highmem-44-highlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by a dedicated 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8481C processor providing 22 physical cores and 44 vCPUs via hyperthreading. The processor features 105 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for vectorized and matrix computations. The instance includes 352 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU, and integrates 19,326 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage across 6 drives without dedicated hardware GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong throughput in multi-threaded decompression, image processing, and cryptographic execution. The server registered 231.48 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and a PassMark CPU encryption score of 38,504.45, both placing within the top 25%. In artificial intelligence tasks, the platform achieves strong performance during small model text generation (310.28 tokens/sec) and medium model prompt processing (181.41 tokens/sec). Conversely, CPU-only large model execution shows substantial limitations, slowing to 2.36 tokens/sec on 70B parameter text generation, which reflects the architectural constraint of relying solely on system memory without discrete GPU accelerators.

General computing benchmarks place the instance within standard operational medians, recording 46,384.24 on the PassMark CPU score, 15,184.0 on Geekbench multi-core, and 36,513.89 on multi-core stress-ng. Uncached memory bandwidth yields 108.68 GB/sec for read operations and 45.23 GB/sec for write operations, alongside support for 50.68 million Redis SET operations per second and 36.68 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Given its combination of extensive NVMe disk capacity and memory-heavy allocation, the z3-highmem-44-highlssd offers distinct qualitative resource density for storage-intensive operations. It is well-fitted for large-scale transactional and NoSQL databases, in-memory caching tiers, data analytics engines, and high-throughput logging systems that require substantial local scratch capacity alongside expansive working memory.
description: Google Cloud Platform z3-highmem-44-highlssd is a storage-optimized virtual server configured with 44 dedicated vCPUs (22 physical cores) on a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8481C processor, 352 GB of RAM, and 19,326 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 system includes 105 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 and AMX extensions. In benchmark assessments, it displays strong performance in cryptographic processing, multi-threaded decompression (231.48 GB/sec), and prompt processing on mid-sized language models, while general compute and memory bandwidth remain in median ranges. Because the machine omits discrete GPUs, large-scale LLM text generation shows lower throughput. With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio coupled with nearly 20 TB of dense local solid-state storage, this server is suitable for high-throughput distributed databases, large-scale indexing, caching tiers, and data analytics pipelines requiring significant IOPS and RAM.
